newsitem.title: USA: Republic Industries to acquire another car group.
newsitem.headline: Republic Industries to acquire another car group.

text.p: Florida billionaire H. Wayne Huizenga's Republic Industries Inc. said Monday it has agreed to acquire the Dobbs Automotive Group of Memphis, Tenn., for $200 million in common stock.
Dobbs is the nation's seventh-largest auto dealer group, with outlets in Tennessee, Alabama, North Carolina, South Carolina, Florida and Arizona, Republic said.
The group includes Honda, Toyota, Lexus, Ford, Nissan, Pontiac, GMC, Mazda, Buick and Mitsubishi dealerships. The acquisition will include all related real estate.

Republic, based in Fort Lauderdale, Fla., is already the nation's largest auto dealer group through just seven months of aggressive acquisitions. Its auto retailing operations include the AutoNation used car superstore chain.
Republic said it has long-term employment agreements to allow Dobbs Chief Executive Officer John Shanks and Chief Operating Officer Frank Grese to continue managing the dealerships.
Republic said it expects to enter similar employment agreements with the rest of Dobbs' senior management team and other employees.
Republic also has subsidiaries in the automotive retailing, automotive rental, automotive financial services, solid waste services and electronic security services industries.

Republic's announcement drew a sharp response from Toyota Motor Sales U.S.A. Inc, the marketing arm of Toyota Motor Corp . Toyota is involved in several legal disputes with Republic over the company's aggressive expansion plans, claiming they may hurt the automaker's retailing image.
The Dobbs purchase involves four Toyota and two Lexus dealerships.

"This latest announcement by Republic of plans to acquire 20 more dealerships suggests that the company has no interest whatsoever in the potential adverse impact of their dealership acquisition binge on consumers, other dealers and the local communities they serve," said Yale Gieszl, executive vice president of Toyota Motor Sales U.S.A.
Republic fell 69 cents to $22.75 in consolidated New York Stock Exchange trading.
